name: Mahli
title: Levite and son of Merari
summary: Mahli was a son of Merari, who was a son of Levi. He was the ancestor of one of the Levitical clans, the Mahlites, which had specific duties related to the transport and maintenance of the tabernacle. His descendants played an important role in temple service throughout Israel's history.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as a son of Merari
keyEvents.description: Mahli is recorded as the firstborn son of Merari, son of Levi, and thus one of the founders of the Levitical clans.

keyEvents.title: The Mahlite clan established
keyEvents.description: The Mahlites were registered as one of the Levitical clans during Israel's wilderness stay, with responsibility for parts of the tabernacle service.

keyEvents.title: Levitical tasks assigned
keyEvents.description: The Mahlites received specific tasks related to transporting the framework, posts, bases, and accessories of the tabernacle during the journey through the wilderness.

keyEvents.title: Counting of the Mahlites
keyEvents.description: The Mahlites were counted as part of the census of the Levites, and their number was recorded in the book of Numbers.

keyEvents.title: Mahlis descendants in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: First Chronicles gives a detailed genealogy of Mahlis descendants, including his sons Eleazar and Kish, and their role in temple service.

keyEvents.title: The service of the Mahlites under David
keyEvents.description: During King Davids organization of temple service, Mahlis descendants were assigned specific roles in worship and service in the temple.
